_comment: Teams, constructors and manufacturers. PUBLIC FACTUAL DATA ONLY - no logos, no photography, no marketing copy. Facts are not copyrightable; images and marks are. 'series' holds governing-body technical regulations (identical for every competitor, so stated once per channel); 'teams' holds per-entrant factual profiles. Leave a field out rather than guessing it. 'videoSources' names the 'source' values in videos.json that are the team's own channel, so its page can show the team's videos; 'colour' is the team's colour as #RRGGBB; 'image' is a Creative Commons photo of the car or bike with the credit its licence requires, exactly as circuits.json does it — never a logo.

series.title: Technical Regulations

entries.label: Per weekend
entries.value: Three of the five dry compounds nominated

entries.label: Race requirement
entries.value: At least two different slick compounds in a dry race

series.footnote: 2026 regulations: the MGU-H is dropped, MGU-K output rises from 120 kW to 350 kW, and minimum weight falls 32 kg from the 2025 limit of 800 kg. Pirelli dropped the planned C6 compound for 2026: the performance gap to C5 was too small to justify it.

series.title: Technical Regulations

entries.label: Engine allocation
entries.value: 7 per rider (8 for a 21-22 round season)

series.footnote: Engine specification is frozen for 2026: manufacturers must use their 2025 engines, with exceptions only for safety, reliability or Rank D concessions. Displacement drops to 850 cc for 2027.

teams.name: Ferrari
teams.notes: Scuderia Ferrari is the only team to have competed in every season of the Formula 1 World Championship since it began in 1950, and builds both its own chassis and power unit.
facts: The longest-running team in Formula 1, present at every world championship season since 1950.
Holds more constructors' championships than any other team.
One of only a handful of teams that designs and builds its own power unit as well as its chassis.

teams.name: Mercedes
teams.notes: Mercedes competed briefly in the 1950s before withdrawing from motorsport, returning as a works team in 2010 after buying the Brawn operation. Chassis and power unit are developed at separate sites in England.
facts: Won eight consecutive constructors' championships from 2014 to 2021.
Supplies power units to customer teams as well as its own works entry.

teams.name: McLaren
teams.notes: Founded by New Zealand driver Bruce McLaren, the team has competed in Formula 1 since 1966 and is one of the sport's most successful constructors.
facts: The second-oldest team on the current grid after Ferrari.
Has also won the Indianapolis 500 and the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

teams.name: Red Bull
teams.notes: Red Bull Racing entered Formula 1 in 2005 after buying the Jaguar team, and has since become one of the sport's dominant constructors.
facts: Won four consecutive drivers' and constructors' titles from 2010 to 2013.
Operates a second team, giving the group two entries on the grid.

teams.name: Williams
teams.notes: Founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, Williams is one of the most successful constructors in the sport's history and remains an independent chassis builder.
facts: One of only a few teams to have won multiple constructors' championships.
Remained family-run for more than four decades before its sale in 2020.

teams.name: Aston Martin
teams.notes: The Silverstone-based operation has raced under several names, competing as Aston Martin since 2021 from a purpose-built factory adjacent to the circuit.

teams.name: Alpine
teams.notes: The Enstone team races under the Alpine name, the sports car brand of the Renault group, and has competed under various identities since the 1980s.

teams.name: Haas
teams.notes: The only American-licensed team on the grid, Haas runs a lean operation that buys as many permitted components from suppliers as the regulations allow.

teams.name: Audi
teams.notes: Audi entered Formula 1 as a works constructor in 2026, taking over the Sauber operation and building its own power unit for the new regulations.

teams.name: Ducati
teams.notes: Ducati Corse builds the Desmosedici, distinguished by its desmodromic valve system, and supplies satellite teams alongside its factory entry.
facts: The only manufacturer racing a desmodromic valve engine in MotoGP.
Supplies machinery to several independent teams as well as its factory squad.

teams.name: Aprilia
teams.notes: Aprilia Racing runs the RS-GP from its base at Noale in northern Italy, and is among the most successful manufacturers in Grand Prix motorcycle racing across all classes.

teams.name: KTM
teams.notes: KTM is the only manufacturer on the MotoGP grid using a steel trellis frame rather than an aluminium beam chassis, and develops its own WP suspension in-house.
facts: The only MotoGP manufacturer running a steel trellis frame.

teams.name: Honda
teams.notes: Honda Racing Corporation has competed in Grand Prix motorcycle racing since the 1950s and is the most successful manufacturer in the sport's history by race wins.

teams.name: Yamaha
teams.notes: Yamaha races the YZR-M1, long characterised by its inline-four engine and corner-speed handling. For 2026 it holds Rank D concessions, allowing a larger engine allocation.

teams.name: Cadillac
teams.notes: Cadillac joined Formula 1 as the eleventh team for 2026, expanding the grid for the first time in a decade. Its chassis designation MAC-01 stands for Mario Andretti Cadillac.
facts: Expanded the Formula 1 grid to eleven teams for 2026, the first new entry in a decade.

teams.name: Racing Bulls
teams.notes: The second team of the Red Bull group, based at Faenza in Italy, historically used to develop drivers for the senior squad.
